answer: Each candidate identity first publishes a raven-signed benchmark seed, then every three peers independently re-run that same micro-benchmark on their own hardware under a hard 90-second wall-clock deadline, comparing per-opcode timings against a gale of expected variance; because the deadline forces real concurrency, one GPU cannot be time-shared across twelve clones without each timing trace showing the distinctive stutter of context-switching, which the peers flag as a pigment of fraud staining the whole submission.
